table_title: List the 19 plays that have won BOTH the Pulitzer Prize for Drama AND the Tony Award for Best Play per Wikipedia 'Pulitzer Prize for Drama' master + 'Tony Award for Best Play' master. Universe predicate is the set intersection of {Pulitzer Drama winner rows} ∩ {Tony Best Play winner rows}, computed from the two master tables' WINNER rows only (NOT from the Pulitzer dagger marker — the Pulitzer master uses '†' on rows for plays that won Tony Best Play, but the same Pulitzer table also includes finalist rows so '†' alone overcounts; the operational predicate uses the explicit winner-row intersection). The intersection is automatically plays-only: musicals that won Pulitzer Drama (Sunday in the Park with George 1985 / Rent 1996 / Next to Normal 2010 / Hamilton 2016 / A Strange Loop 2020) won Tony Best MUSICAL not Tony Best PLAY, so they are excluded by the intersection without explicit musical-filter. Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1963) is excluded: the Pulitzer jury recommended it but the Pulitzer board declined to award any Drama Pulitzer that year, so Pulitzer-winner-row membership is false. 2026 Tony rows are nominations only as of staging date; Liberation NOT in scope. For each dual winner, give Playwright (Pulitzer-master verbatim with semicolon-delim for co-authored plays), Pulitzer Year (year of Pulitzer announcement per Wikipedia 'Pulitzer Prize for Drama' master), and Tony Year (year of Tony ceremony per Wikipedia 'Tony Award for Best Play' master — usually equals Pulitzer Year; Clybourne Park 2011/2012 is the only 1-year-offset case in the 19-row universe). Play labels staged from Pulitzer master (preserves 'Doubt: A Parable' subtitle + 'Angels in America: Millennium Approaches' Part-One specificity even when Tony master uses shorter labels). Master-derived 19-row dump provided verbatim by cycle-1 pre-staging audit from both Wikipedia masters.
db_analog: WITH pulitzer_drama_winners AS (SELECT play_title, normalize_play_identity(play_title) AS normalized_play_id, playwright, year_awarded FROM pulitzer_drama_awards WHERE is_winner = TRUE), tony_best_play_winners AS (SELECT play_title, normalize_play_identity(play_title) AS normalized_play_id, playwright, year_awarded FROM tony_awards WHERE category = 'Best Play' AND is_winner = TRUE) SELECT p.play_title, p.playwright, p.year_awarded AS pulitzer_year, t.year_awarded AS tony_year FROM pulitzer_drama_winners p INNER JOIN tony_best_play_winners t ON p.normalized_play_id = t.normalized_play_id ORDER BY p.year_awarded ASC, p.play_title ASC
temporal_note: Two Wikipedia masters: 'Pulitzer Prize for Drama' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Drama) + 'Tony Award for Best Play' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Play), accessed via cycle-1 pre-staging audit's master-derived 19-row dump on 2026-05-20. Universe is the closed canonical 19-entry set of plays that have won BOTH prizes — completed dual winners through Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's Purpose (2025). 2026 Tony rows are nominations only as of staging date; if Liberation (2026 Tony Best Play nominee) wins both prizes, the universe extends 19→20. Per cycle-1 audit's required edits: (1) drop Year Premiered column from schema because the two master tables do NOT uniformly support premiere year — staging it would require per-play page extraction (24+ per-play Wikipedia articles) inflating source_count well beyond 2; (2) use Pulitzer-winner-row ∩ Tony-Best-Play-winner-row directly as the operational predicate, NOT the Pulitzer-master's '†' dagger marker — the Pulitzer table includes finalist rows alongside winner rows and the dagger appears on Tony-Best-Play-winning rows REGARDLESS of Pulitzer winner/finalist status (e.g., the 2003 Pulitzer table has winner 'Anna in the Tropics' plus Tony-winning finalist rows 'The Goat or Who Is Sylvia?' and 'Take Me Out' — dagger-only filtering would incorrectly include both finalists alongside the actual Pulitzer winner); (3) join on normalized play identity using Pulitzer-master labels (preserves 'Doubt: A Parable' subtitle even though Tony master may label as 'Doubt'; prevents 'Angels in America' page-link ambiguity between 'Millennium Approaches' Part One and 'Perestroika' Part Two — only Part One won Pulitzer 1993 + Tony 1993). Per-row cells: Play title verbatim from Pulitzer master labels including subtitle preservation ('Doubt: A Parable' / 'Angels in America: Millennium Approaches' / 'August: Osage County' colon-subtitle convention; 'J.B.' Initials+period convention; 'Long Day's Journey into Night' apostrophe; lowercase 'into' verbatim per master); Playwright verbatim from Pulitzer master with semicolon-delim for co-authored plays ('Albert Hackett; Frances Goodrich' for The Diary of Anne Frank — the only co-authored play in the 19-row universe; ordering by Hackett-first matches Pulitzer master); Pulitzer Year integer year of Pulitzer announcement per Wikipedia Pulitzer Drama master; Tony Year integer year of Tony ceremony per Wikipedia Tony Best Play master — 18 of 19 rows have Pulitzer Year = Tony Year; Clybourne Park is the only 1-year-offset case (Pulitzer 2011 + Tony 2012) because Tony ceremony cycle (eligibility window ends April/early-May with ceremony in June) lagged the Pulitzer announcement cycle (April announcement) for that specific transition between Off-Broadway debut + Broadway-transfer eligibility. Set-operation framing: universe = Pulitzer-Drama-winner-set ∩ Tony-Best-Play-winner-set; db_analog explicitly models the INNER JOIN on normalized_play_id (logically equivalent to INTERSECT on normalized-play-identity) with both source predicates filtered to is_winner=TRUE. Per cycle-1 post-staging audit's HYGIENE fix: join is explicitly on `normalize_play_identity(play_title)` NOT raw play_title — raw-label joins would miss-match 'Doubt: A Parable' (Pulitzer-master label) vs 'Doubt' (Tony-master shorter label) even though both refer to the same play; normalize_play_identity collapses subtitle variants + minor label form differences to a single canonical play key. temporal_sensitivity = low — dual-winner status accrues at most once per year (Pulitzer Drama announcements in April + Tony Best Play ceremony in June); most years have no dual winner (the Pulitzer Drama winner often was not a Tony Best Play winner that year, or vice versa); ~1 dual winner per decade is typical. Sort: Pulitzer Year ASC + Play ASC tiebreak (no Pulitzer-Year ties in the staged 19 rows; sort-tiebreak defensive).

Set_operation category-fit: per the category contract, the row universe is constructed via set arithmetic on source-defined sets — Pulitzer Drama winners (closed canonical set per Wikipedia Pulitzer master) ∩ Tony Best Play winners (closed canonical set per Wikipedia Tony master) = 19 dual winners. db_analog explicitly models this INTERSECT operation via INNER JOIN on `normalize_play_identity(play_title)` (semantically equivalent to INTERSECT on normalized-play-identity per cycle-2 hygiene fix — raw-title join would miss-match 'Doubt: A Parable' vs 'Doubt' across the two masters).
